newsitem.title: CHINA: China packaging sector seen facing oversupply.
newsitem.headline: China packaging sector seen facing oversupply.

text.p: China's packaging sector is facing oversupply and sliding profits due to a rise in the number of new manufacturers in the market, the China Daily said on Monday.
China had about 15,000 packaging companies, many of them set up in coastal areas by local officials eager to profit from the once-booming sector, the newspaper said.
The sector had grown by an average of 10 percent a year since 1981 and notched up an output value of 126 billion yuan ($15.2 billion) last year, up from 114.5 billion yuan the year before, it added.
The newspaper said oversupply was most evident in aluminium can production and paper packaging.
China's 35 aluminium can makers had a production capacity of 15 billion cans a year but were turning out only half that amount, it said.

"Paper packaging has also faced such a problem -- and as a result, some companies saw their profit margin falls to less than five percent," it quoted Xie Rongquan, vice-president of the China Packaging Technology Association, as saying.
Packaging firms should move from the eastern coastal areas to poorer inland regions, Xie said. He did not say whether the state would give incentives for firms to move.
Poor quality was also a problem, with losses from improper packaging estimated as high as 42 billion yuan a year, the newspaper said.
China imported 200,000 tonnes of aluminium materials a year to make cans, while imports of paper pulp for packaging were 1.0 million tonnes a year, it said. It gave no further details.
